Hover Typing-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Dedicated typing-window marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Hover Typing workflows — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Hover Typing vs Hover Text vs Typing Feedback

US pages use "Hover Typing", "Dedicated typing window", or "Typed characters appear while typing." China storefront copy often uses 悬停键入 or 悬停输入 for Apple's Accessibility feature name, 专用输入窗口 when pointing to the floating typing window, or 键入放大显示 for enlarged typed-character display — depending on whether you mean system Hover Typing, in-app typing-window demos, or trackpad and mouse workflows. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope and avoids conflating Hover Typing with 悬停文本 (Hover Text pointer-hover magnification), 键入反馈 (Typing Feedback keyboard speech), or 全键盘访问 (Full Keyboard Access) when your screenshots show dedicated typing windows, not pointer-hover text overlays or spoken keyboard feedback.

Hover Typing vs Hover Text

Hover Typing (悬停键入 / 悬停输入) shows typed characters in a dedicated typing window while you type. Hover Text (悬停文本) shows enlarged text near the pointer when hovering on existing on-screen text — related accessibility surfaces with different screenshot vocabulary. Do not reuse Hover Text framing on Hover Typing toggle frames unless that is what the screenshot depicts.

Pointer devices vs touch-only marketing

Hover Typing marketing often pairs with iPad trackpad, mouse, Mac pointer, or external pointing device badges. zh-Hans copy should name pointer-device support only when your English listing and screenshots already claim it — not imply universal Hover Typing on touch-only iPhone workflows when your gallery shows trackpad-specific art.

Typing-window demos vs Hover Text magnification galleries

Screenshot galleries for Hover Typing often show dedicated typing-window overlays and activation modifier badges — not side-by-side Hover Text pointer-magnification previews or Typing Feedback speak-as-you-type toggles. Match caption vocabulary to the surface your gallery actually markets; pointer-hover magnification copy belongs on Hover Text listings, not Hover Typing typing-window frames.

AppLocale FAQ

Does AppLocale implement Hover Typing APIs or dedicated typing-window code?

No. We deliver Connect listing metadata copy only — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot caption lines. Hover Typing OS integration, typing-window UI engineering, pointer hover detection for typing, and Settings deep-link engineering are outside scope.

How is Hover Typing listing copy different from Hover Text, Typing Feedback, or Full Keyboard Access?

Hover Typing listing copy covers typed characters appearing in a dedicated typing window while you type — under Settings → Accessibility → Hover Typing. Hover Text covers enlarged text near the pointer when hovering on existing on-screen text (悬停文本). Typing Feedback covers spoken keyboard feedback under Spoken Content. Full Keyboard Access covers navigating the entire UI with a hardware keyboard. Those are different buyer stories with different screenshot vocabulary.

How is Hover Typing different from Hover Text on the product page?

Hover Typing shows typed characters in a dedicated typing window while you type. Hover Text shows enlarged text near the pointer when hovering on existing on-screen text — pointer-hover magnification, not a typing window. If your English listing mentions both, zh-Hans copy should name each workflow accurately per screenshot frame — Hover Text copy belongs on the Hover Text listing guide.

How is this different from Dictation, Voice Control, or Sticky Keys?

Dictation covers speech-to-text input. Voice Control covers spoken UI commands. Sticky Keys covers latching modifier keys for hardware keyboard users. Hover Typing covers a dedicated typing window showing typed characters near the pointer — a different framing on the product page.
